brief: 6 pricing moves that quietly compounded my revenue while I stopped discounting.

slots.subtitle: Six quiet structural moves that compound revenue by selling value instead of cutting prices.
slots.preview1: How decoy tiers lifted my average revenue
slots.preview2: Why killing the free plan filtered my best customers
slots.preview3: The annual switch that cut churn by half overnight

slots.title: Add a
slots.subtitle: A high-priced anchor makes your core plan feel like a steal instead of a stretch.
slots.insight1Body: Customers instinctively avoid the cheapest and most expensive options presented.
slots.insight2Body: Labels like 'Enterprise' signal value without requiring extra features immediately.
slots.insight3Body: Within thirty days, seventy percent of new sign-ups chose the mid-tier plan.
slots.pullQuote: The best tier isn't designed to sell; it's designed to make the middle tier inevitable.

slots.title: Remove the
slots.subtitle: Charging from day one attracts buyers who value the product and support its roadmap.
slots.insight1Body: Free users consumed support hours but rarely converted to paid accounts.
slots.insight2Body: A fourteen-day paid trial outperformed freemium by every meaningful metric.
slots.insight3Body: Paid-only feedback proved sharper and led to faster product iterations.
slots.pullQuote: When you stop giving away the farm, you finally hear from the farmers who matter.

slots.title: Push for
slots.subtitle: Upfront annual plans improve cash flow and handcuff churn before it can start.
slots.insight1Body: Frame it as twelve months for the price of ten, never as a discount.
slots.insight2Body: Pre-select annual billing during checkout to anchor commitment from the start.
slots.insight3Body: Upfront cash funded ads that compounded growth within the same quarter.
slots.pullQuote: Annual cash up front is the cheapest growth capital a founder will ever find.

slots.title: Productize your
slots.subtitle: Break premium features into add-ons so buyers expand without negotiating discounts.
slots.insight1Body: Charge for reporting, white-label, or priority support as separate modules.
slots.insight2Body: A lower entry price reduces sticker shock while preserving expansion revenue.
slots.insight3Body: Self-serve add-ons outsold bundled upgrades by twenty-two percent.
slots.pullQuote: Every feature you give away is a revenue line you can never get back.

slots.title: Grandfather loyal
slots.subtitle: Honor existing customers while increasing prices for new sign-ups without guilt.
slots.insight1Body: Publish a thirty-day warning so no one feels ambushed by the new rate.
slots.insight2Body: Cite new features and outcomes, never inflation or internal costs.
slots.insight3Body: New cohorts paid forty percent more with identical sales cycle lengths.
slots.pullQuote: Loyalty is keeping old prices; courage is charging what the product is worth today.

slots.title: Price by
slots.subtitle: Switch from per-seat to outcome metrics so revenue rises with customer success.
slots.insight1Body: Charge a percentage of value created so customers only pay when they win.
slots.insight2Body: More users no longer mean more friction, which accelerates internal adoption.
slots.insight3Body: Usage-based billing quietly doubled expansion revenue within two quarters.
slots.pullQuote: When your price is tied to their victory, selling stops feeling like taking.

slots.ctaBody: Pricing is a product. Build it deliberately and revenue compounds without ever cutting a price.
